stories.headline: Two chemists share the Nobel Prize for molecular handedness
stories.summary: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has gone to two scientists who untangled a perplexing puzzle about the handedness of molecules. Henri Kagan, of the University of Paris-Sud, and Kenso Soai, of the Tokyo University of Science, were named Nobel laureates on October 7. Their work allows drugmakers to develop safer, more precisely targeted medicines.

stories.headline: Indonesia stops clearing forest to grow more rice
stories.summary: Indonesia has halted a programme to clear millions of hectares of forest for rice cultivation. The government says the country has achieved rice self-sufficiency and no longer needs the extra land. It plans instead to increase yields on existing farmland through improved agricultural methods.

stories.headline: OpenAI publishes 377 results on unsolved maths problems
stories.summary: OpenAI has released 377 results on open problems in mathematics. They fall in areas such as algebra, number theory, combinatorics and theoretical computer science.

stories.headline: Webb looks for Mars-sized worlds smashing together
stories.summary: Astronomers are using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope to investigate young star systems that appear to be experiencing violent events. One of the most important events in the early solar system was a colossal collision between the young Earth and a Mars-sized body known as Theia, and these systems may be going through something similar. Only about 1% of young stars display observable signs of the stage.
